MN202611_evto7ppnlf.t:
Rainbow laces were a common sight for several years across football and other sports

Warning: this article contains offensive language

Homophobia and transphobia are on the rise in English football, with new data revealing record numbers of discrimination reports in the game - so what is the Premier League doing about it?

Last season, with little fanfare, the league introduced a new LGBTQ+ celebratory activation in February, Premier League With Pride.

The lowkey launch contrasts with the landscape of a few years ago, when England internationals like Jordan Henderson and Conor Coady were proudly proclaiming their allyship.

"The one thing it [Premier League With Pride last season] was lacking was engagement from players," said Jon Holmes, founder and lead of news organisation and campaign group Sports Media LGBT.

"Not only would you have the rainbow armbands, but clearer allyship from players - that was more around the late 2010s. That has been in decline."

A report last month from anti-discrimination charity Kick It Out says they received a new high of 1,744 discrimination reports during the 2025-26 season, a 25% increase on the previous campaign. In this, reports of homophobia rose 46% to 203.

Kick It Out said it had received 142 reports of discriminatory mass chanting during the season, a 41% increase on 2024-25 and the highest number recorded. These reports included increases in homophobic and transphobic chants.

A prime example is the 'rent boy' chant predominantly aimed at Chelsea players and fans, for which incidents had dropped since it was criminalised in 2022. However, the combined 24 reports of homophobic chanting in 2025-26 season were the most in three years.

According to Kick It Out, , external many of the incidents over the past few seasons can be linked to domestic and world events, such as the Supreme Court ruling on gender leading to the FA's ban on transgender women in the women's game, which it says led to a spike in transphobic abuse.

The first Premier League With Pride event included rainbow branding at grounds - but nothing involving players

BBC Sport asked all 20 Premier League clubs what diversity policies they have regarding the LGBTQ+ community, and how much of their budget is dedicated to such schemes.

Nine clubs responded to the BBC request. None said how much money they invest in these areas.

A Nottingham Forest spokesperson told BBC Sport: "The club commits significant funding to this important area, and has an Equality, Diversity and Inclusion lead whose role is dedicated to ensuring inclusion is at the heart of everything we do."

Some clubs do visibly engage with their local LGBTQ+ community. Leeds United have been a sponsor of the city's Pride celebrations since 2018. Luke Ayling, then Leeds captain, marched in the Pride parade in 2022.

Brighton are annually represented in their city's extensive Pride events, as are the Manchester clubs.

Manchester City host an annual Progress flag-raising ceremony, while Manchester United said staff marched in the city centre parade. They also ran a flag competition with LGBTQ+ supporters' club Rainbow Devils, with the winning design displayed at Old Trafford for all matchdays.

Tottenham said that at the start of 2024, Spurs in the Community helped launch a weekly football session for members of the LGBTQ+ community.

And for the first time this season, all 20 current Premier League clubs have dedicated fan groups for LGBTQ+ supporters.

"It feels like there is a renaissance in the LGBT fan movement," said Holmes. "There is a rise in homophobia, but it does seem like the authorities are sitting up and taking notice. We can feel a degree of optimism."

But it is difficult for Premier League teams to encourage LGBTQ+ allyship and diversity, when representation within clubs is a mixed bag at best.

According to Kick It Out, which gathered data on the senior management teams from 17 out of the 20 current Premier League clubs, just 0.3% of people in those roles openly identify as LGBTQ+ - well below the UK population average according to latest national census data, with 4% of the British population identifying as LGBTQ+.

At a senior coaching level, from 11 clubs which responded there is no-one from the LGBTQ+ community.

Kick It Out says, comparing the dataset to relevant census data, that if true diversity in football's workforce were to be achieved, over 100 more people from the LGBTQ+ community would have to be employed at Premier League clubs.

The Premier League previously had a high profile association with LGBTQ+ charity Stonewall's Rainbow Laces campaign - but this was ended before the 2025-26 season

Rainbow Laces started in 2014-15 as a collaboration between Stonewall, Paddy Power and the Premier League. For two game weeks, usually around the end of November, players would wear rainbow-coloured laces or armbands, and the colourful branding would be seen in grounds and on broadcast idents.

Holmes said by the end it was doing more harm than good.

"I think the novelty of Rainbow Laces wore off," he told BBC Sport. "It also became more newsworthy to talk about the controversies; it became more difficult for players to engage without difficult questions.

"Also, club media departments are more risk averse, given growing toxicity on social media.

"It has been misconstrued that players were forced to engage, I think it was because Rainbow Laces became de rigueur, and it was perceived that captains would need to lead with the armband and allyship."

Rainbow armbands were introduced in 2017 for captains, having first been worn by MLS club Orlando City following the mass shooting at Pulse, an LGBTQ+ nightclub, in the city in 2016.

But the Premier League held its final Rainbow Laces campaign from 29 November to 5 December, 2024, and it was surrounded by controversy.

Marc Guehi, then Crystal Palace captain, wrote 'I Love Jesus' on his armband in what was widely viewed as a protest against wearing the armband (which was not mandatory).

Ipswich captain Sam Morsy refused to wear the armband, while Manchester United scrapped plans for a Rainbow Laces-themed jacket during the pre-match ceremonies following an objection by Noussair Mazraoui.

Simon Blake, CEO of Stonewall, admitted to BBC Sport that by the end of its 12-year lifespan in the Premier League, Rainbow Laces in that form had run its course.

"When it started, getting a few people to wear the laces was success," he said. "When it ended, when a few people didn't wear them there was criticism.

"If a campaign no longer has a positive vibe, perhaps it is time to do something different.

"Everything must evolve and change, but visibility still matters, it is important not to throw the baby out with the bathwater."

Stonewall held its first ever Rainbow Laces Day on 8 October this year, to encourage LGBTQ+ people to engage with sport. It had no connection with the Premier League.

Marc Guehi and Crystal Palace did not face any action after he wrote on his rainbow armband

It is notable that the players most ardently against Rainbow Laces were also vocal in their religious beliefs.

Guehi has spoken of the importance in his life of his faith and was one of several devout Christian players in the Crystal Palace dressing room. Both Morsy and Mazraoui are practicing Muslims.

Both Holmes and Blake acknowledge that this may have had an impact on Rainbow Laces.

"The influence of religion is clearly quite significant, but I think more understanding is coming in too," said Holmes.

"We have seen many parts of life less willing to engage with Pride, and football reflects that. The nature of LGBT campaigns is peaks and troughs, and we are in a trough."

"We don't have any specific data about what people's beliefs and views are, but we are in a world where people have different views, even within religions themselves," added Blake.

"The important thing is about behaviours, and we must learn to live with people who have these different beliefs and respect them.

"I don't want to speculate, as it would be too easy to assume people of faith would not be inclusive, I know from my work across 30 years that is not true; I have worked with many religious people who are LGBTQ+ supportive. Freedom of belief is important."

The current picture is a difficult one for gay and trans people in football at all levels.

The grassroots game is where the bulk of the increase in abuse has occurred, says Kick It Out, which claims it received 140% more reports last year than in the 2024-25 season. Three quarters of these reports are from senior grassroots games, where the players are over 18.

Away from football, research by Stonewall published in October found 11% of LGBTQ+ people in the UK avoid the gym, exercise classes or sports groups for fear of discrimination. Among trans people, the figure rises to 29%.

It said 15% of LGBTQ+ people who had been to a live sporting event, or watched sport in a bar, in the past year had experienced discrimination there. This rose to 26% for trans people.

"What we know is that there is a lot of work going on around equality and diversity; we also know homophobia and transphobia continue to be rife," Blake said.

"We are in a world, whether at Premier League or grassroots football, where views that may have been perceived to be unacceptable are now being expressed freely. That influences peoples' relationship with sport."

Premier League With Pride will return in 2026-27.

"The matchday activations take place in February in line with LGBTQ+ History Month, when the league and clubs will showcase their commitment to LGBTQ+ inclusion," a Premier League spokesperson told BBC Sport.

"There will be two match rounds dedicated to Premier League With Pride. This means all 20 clubs have a home game during that period, providing an opportunity to highlight and celebrate the LGBTQ+ community in football and showcase the work undertaken to make the game more inclusive.

"There is no centralised activation lined up for November."

The drugs agency described the seized package as a "potent strain of cannabis"

A basketball player from the US has been arrested in Nigeria with 33.95kg (75lbs) of cannabis in his luggage at the main airport in Lagos.

The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) identified the player as Greene Da'monte Khiree, 28, from the US state of Georgia, who it said had arrived from Thailand via the United Arab Emirates.

According to the agency, the suspect said he had been playing professional basketball in Thailand and was visiting to Nigeria to "build networks" for his career. He has not publicly commented on the allegations.

The agency said an examination of the suspect's phone had pointed "to his knowledge of and involvement in the drug trafficking activity".

In statement on Sunday, the agency said he was arrested on Wednesday after airport officials noticed him abandoning his two checked-in bags and attempting to leave with his carry-on bag.

The two bags, which bore his name, contained 32 packs of the drug known as "Loud", a potent strain of cannabis, the agency said.

A tracking device was also recovered from the bags, the agency added.

The International Basketball Federation (FIBA) lists a player by the name Damonte Greene, with the most recent appearance at the Phuket Elite Cup in Thailand, on 26 September.

Nigeria, once regarded primarily as a transit hub for drug trafficking, has increasingly become a producer, consumer, and distributor of illegal drugs, according to the UN.

Recent NDLEA operations have uncovered several industrial-scale methamphetamine laboratories, raising concerns about links between Nigerian drug producers and Mexican cartels seeking to manufacture and export the drug.

In September, the agency said it had dismantled a meth lab and arrested a Mexican suspected drug kingpin who was allegedly attempting to flee Nigeria through Lagos.

Methamphetamine, commonly known as meth, is a highly addictive synthetic drug that can cause severe psychosis, heart attacks or stroke.

In August, a social media influencer suspected of links to an international drug trafficking network was arrested after the authorities seized cocaine worth nearly $28m (£21m), which was destined for the UK.

Alice Huang, ukekwaho kuba intasi y'Ubushinwa kandi wakundanye mu ibanga na Jensen Huang wahoze ayobora sosiyete ya Nvidia, yasezeye ku mwanya w'ubuyobozi muri sosiyete ya Megaspeed muri Kanama (8) mu 2025, nk'uko iyo sosiyete yabitangaje.

Ibi bitangajwe, mu gihe hakomeje ibibazo bivugwa kuri Nvidia nyuma y'amakuru yavugaga ko Jensen Huang yagiranye umubano wihariye na Alice Huang ndetse n'umwe mu bakozi b'iyo sosiyete ikora ibikoresho (chip) byifashishwa mu ikoranabuhanga ry'ubwenge buhangano (AI).

Megaspeed, sosiyete ifatwa nk'umuguzi mukuru wa chip za Nvidia muri Aziya y'Amajyepfo y'Iburasirazuba, ikaba ikomeje gutungwa agatoki ko yaba yaraguze Chips zakozwe na Nvidia mu buryo butemewe, binyuze mu mubano abayobozi b'ibigo byombi bari bafitanye.

Megaspeed yatangaje ko yatangije iperereza ryayo ryihariye, kuri ibyo birego birimo kuyivugwaho.

Yavuze ko raporo zigaruka ku bucuruzi bwayo, uruhererekane rw'itangwa ry'ibikoresho ndetse n'ibikorwa byayo ku rwego mpuzamahanga, zidafite ibimenyetso bifatika.

Yongeyeho ko ibikorwa byayo bikorwa mu buryo bwemewe n'amategeko kandi ko yashyizeho itsinda ry'abanyamategeko bo hanze y'icyo kigo, kugira ngo rikore iperereza ryimbitse.

Gusa ikigo cyo muri Amerika gisesengura ku bibazo by'umutekano, C4ADS, kivuga ko n'ubwo Alice Huang yari yaravuye ku buyobozi bwa Megaspeed, yakomeje kugira uruhare rukomeye mu mikorere yayo.

C4ADS yavuze ko Huang yakomeje kuba afite ijambo rikomeye muri sosiyete nyuma yo kuva ku buyobozi bwayo ku mugaragaro.

Amakuru ya BBC Gahuza ako kanya kuri WhatsApp yawe

Muri Gashyantare(2) 2025, Alice Huang yakorewe iperereza n'abategetsi ba Singapore mu rwego rw'igenzura ryakorwaga kuri Megaspeed n'izindi sosiyete muri rusange.

Ku ruhande rwa Amerika, umudepite John Moolenaar yavuze ko Jensen Huang yemeye kuzitaba komite za Kongere zirimo gukora iperereza ku birego bifitanye isano n'u Bushinwa n'ikoranabuhanga rya AI.

Moolenaar yavuze ko ubwo buhamya buzafasha gusobanukirwa niba hari amakuru y'ibanga yaba yaratanzwe, n'uruhare uwo mugore ukekwaho ubutasi yaba yaragize ku byemezo bya Nvidia bijyanye n'ikoranabuhanga ry'ubwenge buhangano ndetse n'amabwiriza agenga iyoherezwa ryaryo mu mahanga.

Iki kibazo cyanakuruye impaka muri Washington, aho Minisitiri w'Imari wa Amerika Scott Bessent yasabye Nvidia gushaka umuyobozi mushya uturutse hanze y'iyo sosiyete.

Megaspeed ikekwaho gufasha ibigo byo mu Bushinwa kugera kuri chip zigezweho za Nvidia binyuze ku bigo byayo bibika kandi bigatunganya amakuru biri muri Maleziya, Indoneziya na Thailand.

Nvidia ntiyemerewe kugurisha chip zayo zigezweho mu Bushinwa bitewe n'amabwiriza ya Amerika agamije kugenzura iyoherezwa ry'ibikoresho by'ikoranabuhanga mu mahanga.

Megaspeed yavuze ko yubahiriza amategeko yose, harimo n'amabwiriza ya Amerika agenga iyoherezwa ry'ikoranabuhanga, ndetse n'amategeko y'ibihugu byose ikoreramo.

Ubushinwa bwo bwahakanye ko Alice Huang ari intasi, bunavuga ko Amerika itagomba gukoresha iki kibazo nk'urwitwazo rwo gukaza ibikorwa byo gukumira iterambere ry'ikoranabuhanga rya AI.

Kugeza ubu, Alice uvugwaho kuba imbarutso ya byose, ntaragira icyo atangaza ku mugaragaro.

MN202611_104ge658bkr.t:
Is Scotland's system limiting Ben Gannon-Doak's threat?

Two years ago, when Scotland defeated Croatia in the Nations League, that November night at Hampden was the dawn of Ben Gannon-Doak .

The then-teenager took £77m Manchester City man Josko Gvardiol to the cleaners and fans demanded the national team be built around the winger.

The Tartan Army's love for him has never faded - it arguably peaked when he stole the show in Scotland's World Cup opening win over Haiti - but it is fair to say they are growing frustrated, arguably on the Bournemouth man's behalf.

Under Sebastien Pocognoli, Gannon-Doak - who turned 21 on Wednesday - has been deployed at right wing-back, a role that demands defensive instincts unnatural to the pacy attacker.

It is already clear the new head coach is wedded to his preferred system, but it is one that is stifling one of Scotland's greatest attacking outlets - even though his final product still leaves a lot to be desired.

As his side prepare to visit Nations League Group B1 leaders Switzerland on Monday needing a win to have any chance of a promotion play-off place, Pocognoli has addressed both concerns - citing he is not uneasy about either - but pundits and punters alike cannot seem to shift their suspicions.

In that 1-0 victory over 10-man Croatia, it was Gannon-Doak's fearlessness in facing one of Europe's most elite and experienced teams that caught the eye.

His electric speed and directness excited a support who had long been crying out for a player with such qualities and the confidence in applying them. A natural winger, if you will.

In Pocognoli's system, though, there is no space for wingers. Something that former Rangers full-back Richard Foster says must "scunner" the wee man.

"When you're a full-back and you get to play wing-back, it's amazing - all of a sudden you are 10-20 yards up the pitch, doing more attacking and you can be a bit more aggressive," he said on BBC Scotland's Sportsound.

"When you ask a winger to do that, most of the time they are absolutely scunnered. They are thinking 'I don't want to go back there'.

Why 'inspiring' Van Gaal influences Scotland head coach Pocognoli

Six goals to go - will McGinn catch Dalglish & Law?

"Looking at the squad [against North Macedonia], the three most exciting players we had - Findlay Curtis, Josh McPake and Gannon-Doak - are all wingers and he didn't bring two on.

"You look at the previous game [against Slovenia] and the difference McPake and Curtis made by coming on and taking players on - it gives everyone a lift.

"As a fan, you want to get excited about what you are watching. We are playing in a shape where we have the most exciting talents on the bench and they can't get on unless you adjust things. I just think he has to change the formation."

Foster is far from the only one wishing for a shift in shape - and not just for Gannon-Doak's benefit. Much has been made about the Scots' options in defence , too, and whether they match-up to the method.

However, it is arguable Gannon-Doak is the biggest casualty of them all.

"I don't think we're getting the best out of Ben," former Scotland captain Scott Brown told BBC Scotland.

"You saw him making so many last-ditch headers on Friday. He's having to add things to his game that he probably hasn't done before, like throw-ins, defending one-v-one."

No need to mention that throw-in, Scott. But that wasn't the only instance where Gannon-Doak looked a little lost. Think the 'Confused Travolta' meme.

While his position is a new worry, his precision with his final product is not.

Almost in a microcosm, Gannon-Doak's play was laid bare when be hurtled to the byeline before winning what turned out to be the match-winning penalty against the North Macedonians on Friday.

"He made a great run for the penalty, but I did think he could have got his shot away a bit earlier and maybe not taken that extra touch," Brown said.

Back in 2024, the wee live-wire was forgiven for not always finding a pal with a pass or choking at crunch time with his final ball.

However, as the years go on and the caps rack up, his shortcomings are still on show. His end product is still largely poor and patience is wearing thin.

"As long as he is high on the pitch and is creating one-v-ones, I am happy," Pocognoli reiterated post his maiden Hampden win.

"With Ben, we know that he is a young age and needs to work on specific things. On Friday night, he had great opportunities.

"We know that he needs to improve on the end product. But he created a penalty and, against Slovenia and North Macedonia away, he created a number of unbelievable one-v-ones. He did that on Friday night as well.

"We know he can be good if we dominate the game and he can get in good positions if we control the ball.

So Pocognoli is comfortable for now. Already that appears to be a running theme for the head coach - even if others are not.

Highlights: Scotland 2-1 North Macedonia

Amatora y'umunyamabanga mukuru mushya w'umuryango w'ibihugu bivuga Igifaransa (Organisation Internationale de la Francophonie, OIF) yasubitsweho umwaka umwe, kubera kubura umukandida uhuriweho n'abanyamuryango, nkuko bitangazwa n'ibiro ntaramakuru AFP, bisubiramo amagambo y'abari hafi y'iyo dosiye, nyuma yuko inama ya OIF irangiye i Phnom Penh, mu murwa mukuru wa Cambodge.

Iyo nama yaranzwe n'ubushyamirane bukomeye hagati ya Repubulika ya Demokarasi ya Congo (RDC) n'u Rwanda, bushingiye ku ntambara mu burasirazuba bwa RDC.

Umunyarwandakazi Louise Mushikiwabo, wari umukandida ushaka manda ya gatatu, azaguma kuri uwo mwanya w'umunyamabanga mukuru wa OIF kugeza habaye andi matora, u Rwanda rutazagiramo umukandida, nkuko abo bavuganye na AFP babivuze.

Isubikwa ry'ayo matora ni bwo bwa mbere ribayeho mu mateka ya OIF, buri gihe yashyiragaho umunyamabanga mukuru wayo hagendewe ku mukandida uhuriweho na bose – Boutros Boutros Ghali, Abdou Diouf, Michaëlle Jean na Louise Mushikiwabo – kuva uwo mwanya washyirwaho mu mwaka wa 1997.

Abaterankunga ba mbere bakomeye ba OIF, ari bo Ubufaransa na Canada, basabye ko habaho ubumwe, ariko nta guhuriza ku mukandida umwe kwabayeho nyuma y'iminsi ibiri haba ibiganiro bikomeye mu muhezo i Phnom Penh, aho rwari rwabuze gica hagati ya RDC n'u Rwanda.

Kinshasa, ishinja u Rwanda gufasha umutwe w'inyeshyamba wa FRN – wahoze ari M23 – mu burasirazuba bw'icyo gihugu, yari yakangishije kuva muri uwo muryango Louise Mushikiwabo, uwuyobora kuva mu 2018, naramuka atorewe indi manda. U Rwanda ruhakana gufasha FRN.

Kuvamo kw'icyo gihugu cya kabiri mu kugira abavuga Igifaransa benshi cyane ku isi (miliyoni 57,3 ) nyuma y'Ubufaransa, byari kuba ari ikintu gikomeye cyane kibaye kuri OIF, isanzwe yaraciwe intege no kuba mu mwaka ushize ibihugu bitatu byo mu karere ka Sahel – Burkina Faso, Mali na Niger – byarayivuyemo.

Abakandida bane ni bo bahataniraga umwanya w'umunyamabanga mukuru wa OIF: Louise Mushikiwabo, Umunye-Congo Juliana Lumumba, akaba ari n'umukobwa wa Patrice Lumumba waharaniye ubwigenge bwa RDC, Dacian Ciolos wahoze ari Minisitiri w'intebe wa Roumanie, na Coumba Ba wahoze ari Minisitiri muri Mauritania.

Ibihugu 53 na leta by'ibinyamuryango bifite uburenganzira busesuye muri OIF (ku bihugu 90 bigize uwo muryango) byahisemo kudatora muri ayo matora yo mu ibanga, no kwiha umwaka umwe wo kubona umukandida uhuriweho kurushaho.

Taarifa Investigative Desk has reliably established from a french source that elections for the next Secretary General of the La Francophonie organisation have been postponed for one year.

“The election of the secretary-general of the International Organisation of La Francophonie (#OIF) was due to take place on Monday, November 16 in Phnom Penh, #Cambodge, but it is reportedly being postponed for a year, according to sources close to the matter,” said France24, a state-owned French holding company.

Radio France International also reported, “lacking consensus, the OIF postpones the election of the secretary-general by one year.”

The decision to delay the election for Secretary General of OIF has been welcomed differently across the Francophonie world.

Over 8,000km away from the boardroom in Phnom Penh, Kigali people are celebrating the decision as a major win against Kinshasa.

Patrick Muyaya, DRC’s Minister of Communication and Media threatened that Kinshasa would bear the consequences of a possible reappointment of the Rwandan official.

“It is precisely very, very unhealthy, once again, on the part of Mrs. Mushikiwabo, from Rwanda, to want to denounce today or to think that France, which is in its role of facilitating consensus, in accordance with the tradition established within the OIF,” Muyaya told TV5MONDE responding to comments from Mushikiwabo’s accusing France of interference in the elections.

The Chairperson of the African Union Commission (AUC), Mahmoud Ali Youssouf said, “the position of Secretary General of the International Organisation of the Francophonie (OIF) is currently the subject of a competition between African and non-African candidates. Africa must remain united to ensure an African victory. Dispersion must be avoided.”

They include Rwanda’s Louise Mushikiwabo, candidate for a third term; the former Congolese minister Juliana Lumumba, daughter of Patrice Emery Lumumba; the Mauritanian Dr Coumba Ba, minister-advisor and special envoy of President Mohamed Ould El-Ghazouani; and the former Romanian Prime Minister Dacian Cioloș.

A heavy storm earlier this month damaged tents and caused widespread flooding

The UK, Australia, Canada and Italy have issued a joint statement urging Israel to "allow immediate, rapid and unimpeded humanitarian access throughout Gaza", where they say the situation on the ground is "dire".

The foreign ministers warn recent floods have brought "further suffering" to the war-torn territory, which recently had its first winter storm.

The statement says 150,000 tents and other vital supplies are being held at the border.

The Israeli military authority which controls the Gaza crossings has said it is co-ordinating with the US-led Board of Peace and the UN on a winter plan, and that 93,000 tents and 8,600 aid trucks with winter supplies had entered the territory.

It added that reconstruction "can only begin after Hamas fully disarms".

The UN Office for the Co-ordination of Humanitarian Affairs said the widespread flooding and a landslide led to a number of deaths, thousands of damaged shelters and the suspension of critical services.

The statement from the British, Australian, Canadian and Italian foreign ministers says , external : "This situation is entirely reversible - and there is still time to act before the winter fully sets in."

"The crossings must be opened, and the tents allowed in. Dual-use items necessary for humanitarian operations and early recovery must be granted entry before it is too late."

The European Union issued a similar statement on Saturday , external , reiterating its "grave concern" over what it called the "persistent and devastating humanitarian crisis".

The EU also urged Israel to comply with international law.

The war in Gaza was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, in which about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others were taken hostage.

Israel responded by launching a military campaign in Gaza, during which more than 74,690 people have been killed, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.

Israeli air strikes and other attacks have continued to take place almost every day despite the ceasefire agreed in October last year.

MN202611_1giw6rwz7sa.t:
PHNOM PENH – The contest over who should lead the International Organization of La Francophonie (OIF) has exposed deep diplomatic divisions within an organization whose founding principle is to bring countries together through a shared language, cooperation and common values.

Rwanda’s Louise Mushikiwabo, whose second term as Secretary-General was due to end, has been granted a one-year extension after heads of state and government failed to reach an agreement on her successor during the summit in Phnom Penh.

The failure to resolve the leadership contest reflects a widening disagreement among member states over how the next Secretary-General should be selected. While one camp pushed for an election, others favored avoiding a vote in favor of reaching consensus on a single candidate.

The OIF recently amended its rules, making an election the preferred method of selecting the Secretary-General.

Under the new system, each member state has one vote, marking a departure from the previous practice, which prioritized consensus and gave considerable influence to major financial contributors such as Canada and France.

The stalemate followed days of intense diplomatic maneuvering, including an unsuccessful attempt by Senegalese President Bassirou Diomaye Faye to persuade President Paul Kagame to withdraw Mushikiwabo’s candidacy.

According to diplomatic reporting by Africa Intelligence, a meeting convened at Faye’s initiative on the evening of November 15 failed to change Rwanda’s position, leaving member states unable to resolve the contest.

A Regional Dispute Enters the Francophonie

The strongest opposition to Mushikiwabo’s re-election came from the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), whose government had put forward former Culture Minister Juliana Amato Lumumba as a candidate.

The Congolese government had also threatened to withdraw from the OIF should Mushikiwabo secure another term, raising the prospect of a major institutional setback for an organization already affected by the departure of Mali, Niger and Burkina Faso in 2025.

In a last-minute change of strategy, the DRC announced its willingness to withdraw Lumumba’s candidacy and support Romania’s Dacian Cioloș, presenting the move as an attempt to find a consensus candidate and prevent the organization from becoming an extension of the Rwanda-DRC confrontation.

However, Rwanda questioned the logic of replacing an African candidate with a European one, particularly in light of an African Union decision adopted in July 2026 endorsing three African candidacies and calling on African OIF members to rally behind one of them.

“The DRC’s announced support for the Romanian candidate Dacian Cioloș, at the expense of the two other African women candidates, is a flagrant violation,” Nduhungirehe said in a statement.

France’s Influence and the Question of Consensus

France, which has considerable influence within the Francophone world as one of the organization’s largest financial contributors, found itself at the center of the diplomatic contest.

Canada, together with its associated provinces, contributes €19.4 million to the OIF, while France contributes €19.3 million.

Their financial contributions have traditionally given them considerable weight in the organization’s affairs, adding another dimension to the debate over how its leadership should be decided.

President Emmanuel Macron reportedly sought to persuade Kagame to withdraw Mushikiwabo’s candidacy, with Paris presenting its intervention as an effort to preserve the organization’s unity.

Rwanda, however, viewed the pressure as interference in a decision that should be left to member states.

The disagreement has revived questions about the extent to which former colonial powers should influence leadership decisions in an organization that brings together countries from Africa, Europe, Asia and the Americas.

The irony is particularly striking given Mushikiwabo’s own warning during the summit’s opening proceedings against allowing bilateral disputes to undermine the organization.

“The OIF is not a defensive alliance, and its unity does not require uniformity of positions. Members should resist turning the organization into a platform for bilateral disputes,” she said.

Its value, she added, lies in the ability of members to meet on an equal footing and turn their diversity into a source of influence and trust.

Macron similarly appealed for unity, warning against internal fractures and arguing that the organization’s strength depended on preserving cohesion among its members.

A Leadership Decision with Wider Consequences

Beyond the contest over one position, the failure to agree on the next Secretary-General raises questions about the future direction and credibility of the OIF.

The organization brings together 90 states and governments, including 53 full members, making it a significant platform for political dialogue, cultural cooperation and international engagement.

Its membership stretches well beyond countries where French is the dominant language, reflecting a broader ambition to build partnerships across continents.

The departure of Mali, Niger and Burkina Faso in 2025 had already demonstrated how political disagreements can weaken that ambition. Losing the DRC, one of the largest French-speaking countries in the world, would further undermine the organization’s continental reach and influence.

For Mushikiwabo, the one-year extension offers continuity after eight years at the helm, but it also leaves the question of her longer-term future unresolved.

The failure to settle the leadership contest has exposed the difficulty of reconciling competing national interests under a system that is increasingly expected to rely on voting rather than consensus.

The question facing the OIF is therefore whether an organization built around linguistic and cultural ties can remain a credible multilateral platform when political rivalries among its members threaten to overshadow the common interests that brought them together.

Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband has called Russell Brand's message in which he claimed he was not guilty of the offences he's been jailed for as "disgusting" and showing "no remorse".

Brand has been convicted of rape and three counts of sexual assault, and is serving a 10-and-half-year sentence. He is currently being held at HMP Littlehey in Cambridgeshire.

His wife Laura read out a message from him on their Sunday Service show on YouTube, in which the convicted rapist claimed: "I am not guilty of the offences I have been jailed for."

The Victims' Commissioner for London, Andrea Simon, told Radio 4's Today programme that Brand's claims of innocence will "certainly retraumatise his victims and other survivors of rape who have to hear it".

Responding to the video, Miliband told Sky News: "His crimes are heinous and awful. I think it's revolting, by the way, that he shows no remorse today in his comments."

"No remorse, no sympathy for the victims. Just disgusting comments," he added.

In her Today interview, Simon added: "The victims during the sentencing hearing highlighted how his denials and ongoing media fame over two decades had added to their pain and trauma," she said.

"The fact survivors are still having to hear this now is really problematic and very concerning that we can't do more to protect them from it."

Russell Brand (pictured during his trial) delivered a message to followers via his wife Laura

The foreign secretary apologised for having appeared on the former comedian's online show in 2015, when he was Labour leader.

On BBC Radio 4's Today programme on Monday, Miliband said if he'd known about the allegations then, he would not have done the interview.

"I deeply regret doing that interview and all my sympathies are with those victims and we should listen to those victims," he said.

Over the weekend, Brand was moved from HMP Wandsworth in south London to Littlehey prison in Cambridgeshire, a prison that mostly houses sex offenders and has tailored programmes for them.

His wife said on the podcast that she had been speaking to him and he "is OK and is praying".

Foreign Office minister Stephen Doughty, told LBC he agreed it was not "a good look" that he'd been moved to a lower security prison.

"I think people want to see him facing the appropriate punishment for what are appalling crimes against women and others and I think the whole episode is shocking," he said.

Gun violence remains a persistent problem in South Africa, where about 60 people are murdered every day, according to police (file photo)

South African police are investigating the murders of 17 people in two separate shootings on Sunday night.

Eight men were fatally shot in a minibus in KwaZulu-Natal province. Police declared them dead when they arrived at the scene. Hours later, nine people were found shot dead inside a shack in western Pretoria.

Police say the two incidents are unrelated. The motive for the shootings has not yet been established.

South Africa is struggling to contain violent crime, including gang-related killings. The country has one of the world's highest murder rates.

Police say they responded to reports of a shooting ⁠outside Pietermaritzburg town in KwaZulu-Natal and found a white seven-seater vehicle riddled with bullet holes.

Inside were eight men with multiple gunshot wounds.

"It has not been established how the incident happened, and police are collecting pieces of evidence to determine the possible motive of the killings and the identity of the suspects," police spokesperson Robert Netshiunda said.

The police have launched a manhunt for the suspects.

In a separate shooting in the Jeffsville informal settlement in Atteridgeville, west of Pretoria, police found the bodies of six men and three women.

They are believed to have been killed inside a four-room shack between 22:00 and 23:00 on Sunday. The bodies were scattered across the rooms, with several spent cartridges discovered outside the shack.

Community members initially mistook the gunshots for thunder and lightning.

"The provincial commissioner of police in Gauteng [province, which includes Pretoria] has mobilized the necessary resources, including the crime intelligence and the deputy provincial commissioner tracking team to search for the suspect," police spokesperson Brigadier Brenda Muridili said.

It's not the first mass shooting in the area. In January, five men were shot dead outside a local shop in broad daylight.

Illegal firearms are widespread in South Africa, where gun violence remains a persistent problem, increasingly involving mass shootings.

In September, 28 people were killed in two separate cases.

Eighteen people were killed when eight gunmen stormed a bar near Johannesburg and opened fire on 25 September. Fourteen others were injured.

In a separate shooting the following day, 10 people were killed outside an entertainment venue in a township near Cape Town. A further 11 were injured.

Much of the violence has been linked to turf wars between gangs involved in drug trafficking and illegal mining.

In February, President Cyril Ramaphosa described organised crime as "the most immediate threat to our democracy, our society and our economic development".

Earlier this year, the military was deployed alongside police to five provinces with the highest murder rates, including Gauteng, in an effort to tackle armed violence.

According to the latest police statistics, 5,427 people were murdered nationwide between April and June 2026, an average of about 60 killings a day. This was a 6% decline compared with the same period a year earlier.

Farrell has won three out of five matches against South Africa as Ireland boss

Head coach Andy Farrell says Ireland will look to draw inspiration from previous big wins under his watch when they renew their rivalry with world champions South Africa this weekend.

Having beaten Argentina and Fiji, Ireland hope to avenge last year's 24-13 defeat by the Springboks when they host Rassie Erasmus' side at Aviva Stadium on Saturday (16:40 GMT).

South Africa arrive in Dublin with a point to prove after being edged out by France in an enthralling heavyweight tussle in Paris on Friday night.

Ireland, who were unconvincing at times in Saturday's 43-15 victory over Fiji, have lost their past six contests against New Zealand, France and South Africa - the three teams above them in the world rankings - by double-digit margins.

However, Farrell has guided Ireland to three wins over the Springboks, including a 2023 Rugby World Cup pool stage success at Stade de France and a last-gasp 25-24 triumph in Durban the following year.

"We know we can do it because we've done it," said Farrell.

"History tells us that as well. We know that when it really matters, we've been able to stand up - not always has that turned out to be a winning result, but we've always showed our mettle against the best and are always up for a challenge.

Five EU countries are expected to announce the creation of a migrant deportation centre in Rwanda, according to diplomatic sources, part of a broader push to boost deportations and curb irregular migration.

Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands are expected to announce a "return hub" located in the landlocked east-central African country's capital Kigali.

The deal follows a recent EU reform that allowed for the creation of such hubs outside of the bloc.

It is understood the scheme would only apply to asylum seekers who had exhausted all legal avenues to remain in the EU, unlike a scrapped 2022 British deal that envisaged sending people to Rwanda to have their claims processed.

Legal challenges meant the UK deal never took off, and it was eventually scrapped by the incoming Labour government in 2024 .

In August, Rwanda confirmed it had begun "preliminary discussions" with several European states.

The Rwanda hub is expected to initially run as a pilot, hosting about 100 people, with each of the five nations possibly sending about 20 migrants, diplomatic sources told the AFP news agency.

The EU countries reportedly expressed hope that a centre would be running in 2027. The United Nations' International Organisation for Migration (IOM) could play an ancillary role.

"IOM has a long history of providing assistance to migrants in situations of transit, including in complex contexts," an IOM spokesperson said, adding the agency was in discussions with some EU countries "on plans for the establishment of return hubs or similar mechanisms".

Human Rights Watch's senior Africa researcher Clementine de Montjoye said the choice of Rwanda would be a cause of concern as it had a "well-established record of repression of dissent, arbitrary detention, ill-treatment in detention" and support for armed rebels in the neighbouring Democratic Republic of Congo.

"Paying Kigali to host a deportation programme would not only cause suffering and harm to those deported, it would finance and provide political leverage to a government responsible for serious human rights abuses at home and abroad."

Allies of Jensen Huang are trying to rally support for the former Nvidia boss to get his job back after resigning last week over a scandal involving extramarital affairs, one involving an alleged Chinese spy.

SpaceX boss Elon Musk and Tim Sweeney, chief executive of Fortnite-maker Epic Games, are among those backing a campaign to get the AI chip giant's board to "Bring Jensen Back".

Huang resigned as chief executive of Nvidia after the emergence of two affairs, one of whom was with a woman suspected of spying for China and another allegedly with one of his employees.

It has created a crisis for one of the world's most valuable firms which is a key part of the AI industry and its huge expansion.

An open letter calling for Nvidia's board to give Huang his job back while an internal probe is conducted has received more than 175,000 signatures, including Musk and Sweeney, according a website named "Stand with Jensen".

The campaign group said it is made up of current and former Nvidia employees, partners, shareholders and supporters.

"We write with gratitude for Jensen Huang and with a clear demand to the board: bring Jensen back while an independent investigation establishes the facts, unless and until you can provide compelling evidence that his removal is in NVIDIA's best interests," the letter said.

Allies of the ex-Nvidia boss wrote they were "concerned that Jensen was removed without meaningful due process".

Huang had been expected to weather the storm following the revelation of an affair involving Alice Huang, alleged to be a Chinese spy.

However, he resigned last Thursday after a second extra-marital relationship emerged, this time allegedly with an executive at Nvidia who reported to him.

The scandal-hit tech boss is now discussing a possible return to Nvidia with confidants, according to Financial Times. , external

The newspaper quoted one ally saying that a "war room" of Silicon Valley executives was being convened to lobby for the former Nvidia boss's reinstatement.

A representative forJensen Huang declined to comment on the report.

The so-called war room also wants to get support for Huang from the White House.

While President Donald Trump recently spoke in glowing terms about Huang , the scandal has created tensions between the US Treasury and Commerce departments over shipments of high-end Nvidia chips to Alice Huang's former firm, Megaspeed.

It has raised questions about the possibility that the chips may have ended up in China despite US export restrictions.

The BBC understands that the likelihood of Huang being reinstated is low while the Nvidia's internal investigations are ongoing.

The FBI is also investigating the affair between the former Nvidia boss and Alice Huang, according to Trump.

Musk claimed that "critical deals" involving Nvidia's technology would be lost following Huang's resignation.

"Jensen drove supply chain brilliantly at Nvidia but many of those deals were a handshake with Jensen, not a written contract.

If Huang was reinstated, it would face scrutiny from Washington. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has called for Nvidia to hire its next chief executive from outside the company.

Shareholders in Nvidia also want Huang back at Nvidia's helm.

In an open letter to the board, Brad Gerstner, founder of Altimeter Capital and Atreides Management boss Gavin Baker called for management to leave "all options on the table, including the potential return of Jensen Huang".

Nicola Packer was acquitted of "unlawfully administering to herself a poison or other noxious thing" with the "intent to procure a miscarriage"

Women arrested or convicted for having illegal abortions will have their criminal records wiped as new automatic pardons come into force in England and Wales , external .

Ending the Victorian-era law should avoid traumatic experiences such as that of Nicola Packer, who was recently cleared by a jury after taking medication at home during a Covid lockdown. She had ended a pregnancy without realising she was around 26 weeks pregnant, far beyond the legal 10 week limit.

Her friend Helle Tumbridge told the BBC's Today Programme she had been "treated appallingly" until justice was served.

Labour MP Tonia Antoniazzi, who brought forward the decriminalisation amendment last year, says the change will clear the names of more than 100 women who have been "unnecessarily harmed" by an "outdated" law.

Ms Packer, who was 41 at the time, took pills called mifepristone and misoprostol, which were prescribed over the phone due to Covid restrictions, to end a pregnancy in 2020.

Prosecutors alleged that she knew she had been pregnant for more than 10 weeks, which she denied.

Jurors deliberated for more than six hours to reach their unanimous verdict, clearing her name.

Speaking with the BBC and Nicola's consent, her friend Ms Tumbridge said the whole incident was "incredibly traumatic".

"Nicky had what's known as a cryptic pregnancy - that's when you don't have any sign of a pregnancy, no baby bump, no other symptoms.

"She thought she was just a few weeks pregnant and she sought an abortion and was prescribed that by the NHS. Unfortunately, she was a lot more far gone."

Nicola experienced a stillbirth and went to hospital. The staff there called the police.

"She was arrested. She spent a time in her hospital room recovering with two police officers present, one was a man. She was treated appallingly. She was made to use the toilet with the door open in front of the police officers."

It took five years of investigations for a trial to eventually find her not guilty.

"Of course, by that point the damage had been done," says Tumbridge, "and she'll live with that trauma for the rest of her life."

At the time, The Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists said Nicola's trial demonstrated "just how outdated and harmful" that law was.

It is now no longer a criminal offence for a pregnant woman to terminate her own pregnancy at any stage.

Women affected do not need to take any action.

Minister for Victims and Tackling Violence Against Women and Girls, Alex Davies-Jones, said pardoning women for abortion offences related to their own pregnancy had been a priority.

"I'm pleased to be able to commence the change that Parliament voted for.

"For those affected, I know that clear and accessible information about what happens next is vital. Women do not have to take any direct action themselves, but can find out more information online and contact our dedicated casework team."

Heidi Stewart, from the abortion care provider BPAS, said: "While no pardon can undo the distress and trauma these women have experienced, this historic change in the law recognises the profound harm caused by their criminalisation and represents a meaningful step towards justice."

Abortion in England and Wales is legal with an authorised provider up to 24 weeks, with very limited circumstances allowing one after this time, such as when the mother's life is at risk or the child would be born with a severe disability.

It is also legal to take prescribed medication at home if a woman is less than 10 weeks pregnant.

Romelu Lukaku has retired from international football, saying he has "enjoyed every single moment" of playing for Belgium.

Fenerbahce striker Lukaku, 33, made his international debut in 2010 and is Belgium's all-time leading men's goalscorer with 94 goals in 135 appearances.

He is the fifth highest men's international goalscorer of all time, behind Sunil Chhetri, Ali Daei, Lionel Messi and leader Cristiano Ronaldo, who has scored 146.

Lukaku scored eight goals across four World Cups, including in the run to the quarter-finals at this summer's tournament, and a total of six goals at three European Championships.

Writing on Instagram, , external the former Everton, Chelsea and Manchester United forward thanked his team-mates and coaches "for pushing and trusting me to help the team" during his 16 years with the national side.

He missed Belgium's Nations League win over Turkey last week with a hip injury and was an unused substitute on Sunday as they qualified for the last eight of the competition by beating Italy 4-1.

"These 16 years I gave all I had for the national team... I went through every emotion possible," Lukaku wrote.

"To the Belgium fans thank you for the support you gave our team. I am proud to have represented my country in four World Cups and three European Championships.

"I will never forget those moments. I'm at peace with my decision to stop here. It was amazing. It was enjoyable. I'm grateful."

In 2023, Lukaku scored 14 times in eight Euro 2024 qualifying appearances, breaking the record for goals scored by a player in a European Championship qualifying campaign.

Buri mwaka tariki ya 16 Ugushyingo, isi yizihiza Umunsi Mpuzamahanga wo Koroherana (International Day for Tolerance), ugamije gushishikariza abantu kubahana, kwemera ko batandukanye no kubana mu mahoro, hatitawe ku mico, imyemerere, ibitekerezo cyangwa inkomoko byabo.

Uyu munsi washyizweho n’Umuryango w’Abibumbye mu 1996, hashingiwe ku itangazo rya UNESCO ryerekeye amahame yo koroherana ryemejwe tariki ya 16 Ugushyingo 1995.

Pasiteri Rutayire Antoine avuga ko koroherana bisobanura kubaha no kwemera ko abantu bashobora kugira ibitekerezo, imyemerere, imico n’imibereho bitandukanye, ariko bagakomeza kubana mu bwubahane. Asobanura ko koroherana bidahwanye no kwemera akarengane cyangwa guceceka imbere y’ihohoterwa, ahubwo ko bisaba kubaha uburenganzira bwa buri muntu no gukemura ibyo abantu batumvikanaho mu mahoro.

Ati: “Abavandimwe, abashakanye, abo bakorana, abiga mu ishuri rimwe n’abaturanyi bose bagomba koroherana kugira ngo aho bari hose haboneke ituze n’umutekano.”

Pasiteri Rutayire avuga ko abantu bagira umuco wo korohera abandi babaho neza, batavunika mu mutima, kuko akenshi baba barangwa no kumva no guha agaciro abandi mu buzima bwabo bwa buri munsi.

Ati: “Ndetse no mu muhanda, iyo tugenda mu modoka, tutoroherana usanga duteza impanuka. Na ho bisaba koroherana kugira ngo urujya n’uruza rw’ibinyabiziga rugende neza.”

Pasiteri Rutayire avuga ko korohera abandi bituma ubuzima bwihuta kandi bukagenda neza. Yatanze urugero rw’abantu batsimbarara ku bitekerezo byabo cyangwa ku byo bashaka, agaragaza ko iyo umugore, umugabo cyangwa umwana adashoboye koroshya mu mibereho ye, akenshi usanga n’imibereho y’umuryango we itagenda neza.

Ati “ Nikimwe no mu kazi iyo hari bamwe batsimbarara ku byabo bituma abandi akazi katagenda neza kubera kwanga kumva ibitekerezo by’abandi”.

Mu gihe isi ikomeje guhura n'ibibazo birimo intambara, amakimbirane, ivangura, urwango n'amacakubiri ashingiye ku moko, imyemerere n'ibitekerezo bya politiki, koroherana bifatwa nk'imwe mu nzira zifasha kubaka amahoro arambye.

UNESCO igaragaza ko kwihanganirana atari ukwirengagiza itandukaniro riri hagati y’abantu, ahubwo ari ukwemera uburenganzira bwa buri wese, kubaha ikiremwamuntu no guharanira ko abantu babana batishishanya.

Ni na yo mpamvu uyu munsi ushimangira akamaro ko kwigisha abana n’urubyiruko umuco wo kubaha abandi, kuganira ku bibazo batumvikanaho no kwirinda imvugo n'ibikorwa bibiba urwango.

Koroherana ntibikwiye kugarukira ku magambo cyangwa ku munsi umwe wahariwe kubizirikana. Bigomba kugaragarira mu mibereho ya buri munsi, mu miryango, mu mashuri, ku kazi no mu mibanire rusange.

Kubaha ibitekerezo by’undi nubwo bitandukanye n’ibyawe, kumutega amatwi, kwirinda kumucira urubanza rushingiye ku byo atandukaniyeho nawe no gukemura amakimbirane binyuze mu biganiro ni bimwe mu bikorwa bigaragaza umuco wo koroherana.

Uyu munsi uributsa abantu ko itandukaniro ridakwiye kuba intandaro y'amacakubiri, ahubwo ko rishobora kuba amahirwe yo kwigiranaho, gusobanukirwa no kubaka umuryango urangwa n'ubumwe n'amahoro.

Germany manager Jurgen Klopp says he "didn't think things could get worse after Sepp Blatter, but someone has managed to do just that" as he called for Fifa president Gianni Infantino to be replaced.

Blatter resigned as Fifa boss in 2015 amid a corruption scandal and was succeeded by Infantino in February 2016.

Infantino plans to stand for re-election in March but has been under pressure since scrapping his Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal, which included selling off stakes in the World Cup and other Fifa competitions to private investors.

Infantino apologised to the Fifa Council for the plan but was told he was not fit to lead world football's governing body unless he released all the documents and answered key questions.

"I've been following football for many years. There are people who are much more knowledgeable about this than I am. But I think most people now agree a change would make a lot of sense," said Klopp.

Former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger, who is Fifa's head of global development, had been considering running for the job but sources have told BBC Sport he has ruled himself out.

Mario Frick arrives at Aberdeen with the Pittodrie side sitting second bottom of the table and a game against relegation rivals Kilmarnock first up.

Lose that match and they fall to the foot of the Scottish Premiership. No pressure.

Apart from the obvious, what is it that the new head coach has to do to restore Aberdeen to previous glory days and avoid becoming yet another managerial failure at Pittodrie?

Okay, maybe this was obvious. But it's Aberdeen's clearest weakness this season.

They have the joint worst attacking record in the league, having only scored 12 goals and routinely looked completely short of confidence in front of goal.

Kevin Nisbet, the club captain, has 14 goals for the season. Nine of those came in the run to the Premier Sports Cup semi-final. Behind him, no-one has more than two.

Most concerning of all is that the Dons' have created the lowest xG (15.3) in the league so far. Not only are they not creating very many quality chances, they're struggling to take them.

They have just 3.3 shots on target per match, with a shot conversion rate of just 7.3%. Both metrics are the worst in the league.

Only Falkirk have created fewer big chances (19 to Aberdeen's 22) - the difference being John McGlynn's side score them.

Getting the best out of Connor Ronan could be key for Mario Frick

One of the most frequent accusations that came predecessor Stephen Robinson's way was that his team lacked an identity and players looked unsure as to the tactical plan they had been told to carry out.

Given the Northern Irishman's clear style of play with St Mirren, that was a surprise.

His team in Paisley were known for their physically-domineering displays that were full of grit and graft. That wasn't the case in the North East.

Frick seemingly prefers a 4-4-2 formation, with the midfield playing in a diamond.

That might be bad news for new signings Tony Yogane and Lewis Smith, wingers who did get a look in under Robinson but struggled to make much of an impact.

Sticking to a consistent midfield will help with that. While Robinson regularly relied on Afeez Aremu in the middle of the park, the head coach often chopped and changed his midfield partner.

Of all of Aberdeen's 15 summer signings, Connor Ronan was the one that probably caused the most optimism. Another former St Mirren man, he impressed in his time in Paisley.

The Irishman won a move to Major League Soccer with Colorado Rapids off the back of that form and was also called up to the Republic of Ireland squad without winning a cap.

Eight goals from midfield in the 2021-22 season was a good return - and a couple of them were screamers.

Former Aberdeen midfielder Jamie McGrath recently reminded his old fanbase that they could do with replacing him after he scored a rocket for Hibs in the 4-0 win that did for Robinson.

Ronan could be the answer, playing in a similar role with the same attacking capabilities.

He has yet to hit the heights at Pittodrie, but if Frick can make him tick, the 28-year-old could fire Aberdeen back up the league table.

James Trafford has made five appearances for England, all of them in 2026

As he was mobbed by his England team-mates for a late double save that secured England's memorable 3-2 win against world champions Spain on Sunday, the debate that followed about who the country's number one is was inevitable.

The Leeds stopper was given his chance to show England boss Thomas Tuchel what he could do again - and he absolutely took it.

On his fifth England cap the 24-year-old enjoyed a magnificent performance in Madrid as his side handed the hosts their first loss in 43 matches.

Trafford made four key saves in the final 12 minutes of the game, including an incredible double stop to first deny a Lamine Yamal curler and then dive again to his right to keep out Fermin Lopez from close range.

Last week England manager Thomas Tuchel had made it clear that Everton goalkeeper Jordan Pickford was his number one.

But after full-time in Spain Tuchel told ITV Sport "there's no number one" and Trafford had "a brilliant match".

So, following his performance on Sunday night, is Trafford now likely to oust Pickford as England's go-to goalkeeper?

Is Trafford 'closing the gap' on Pickford?

Despite being just 24 years old Trafford has already been England's most expensive goalkeeper by transfer fee... twice.

Trafford returned to his boyhood Manchester City from Burnley for a £31m fee in 2025 and then left the Etihad for Leeds for £45m this summer - having been limited to being Pep Guardiola's 'cup goalkeeper'.

Given the downturn in form of their current goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma, many City fans may well be wishing Trafford had stayed. Their loss is Leeds' - and maybe England's - gain.

At Leeds he has found his form and this season ranks first among the 52 goalkeepers who have played at least 10 games in Europe's big five leagues by save percentage (81.4%).

He has made five appearances for England, all of them in 2026, and has rotated with Pickford across the Three Lions' five matches since the World Cup.

Pickford has started against Czech Republic and Croatia twice whereas Trafford has played against Czech Republic and started both England's matches with Spain, home and away.

After England's win in Madrid, which was the first time Spain had lost in the city in 39 years, Trafford's double-save was praised by his Three Lions team-mate Declan Rice.

"Everything happened so quick so for him to make two in the space of two seconds is massive," he told ITV. "A massive night for him."

Spain manager Luis de la Fuente agreed. He said: "We did generate some chances but England's goalkeeper has produced a fantastic performance and stopped two or three potential goals in the last 10 or 15 minutes."

After the double-save several England players ran over to celebrate with Trafford.

And on Tuchel's decision to rotate between his two keepers former Manchester United captain Roy Keane told ITV: "I think it's smart management.

"This is the perfect time for Trafford to come in, against top players, and show what he's capable of doing."

Social media has been full of the 'England number one' debate since, with many suggesting this was a moment that marked the changing of the guard.

Could Tuchel really now not start with Trafford for England's Nations League quarter-finals? Only time will tell.

What about Jordan Pickford though? England's undisputed first choice for almost 10 years has rarely let his country down.

Pickford, 32, has won 94 caps for England since making his debut in a 0-0 draw with Germany in 2017 and during his time as number one England have reached two World Cup semi-finals and two Euros finals.

According to Opta stats, Pickford has only made two errors leading to goals across his England career, with 46 clean sheets and a 74.3% save ratio.

And since the start of the 2024-25 season, only Arsenal's title-winning keeper David Raya has more clean sheets in the league than Pickford at Everton.

"We saw the last selections and all thought Jordan Pickford's place is under threat and James Trafford is going to be the next number one. I don't think Thomas Tuchel saw it as starkly or simply as that," said former England number one goalkeeper Paul Robinson to BBC Sport before England's win against Spain,

"It's a conversation that will definitely take place down the road, but not now. Jordan is England's first choice, in my opinion, rightfully so given his consistency and performances over such a long period.

"This is a debate and conversation for the future definitely because Father Time catches up with everyone eventually and the manager needs to have a contingency plan, but Jordan Pickford very much remains number one and Thomas Tuchel has said as much.

"I don't think Jordan Pickford is under threat for his jersey on a permanent basis any time soon, irrespective of the next selection."

This isn't a debate that is going away any time soon. But having two goalkeepers genuinely competing for that number one shirt can only be to England's benefit.

Iyo havuzwe ubukoroni mu Burundi, benshi bashobora guca babona Ububirigi gusa.

Izo mva ziri muri zone Rugombo, mu yahoze ari intara ya Cibitoke, ubu iri mu ntara yagutse ya Bujumbura mu buraruko bushira uburengero bw'Uburundi.

Izo mva zashinguwemwo Abasirikare b'Abadagi n'Abanyafrika barwanira intwaro y'Ubudagi.

Nk'uko bivugwa na Jean Berchmans Ndihokubwayo, umuhinga mu vya kahise akaba n'umwigisha muri kaminuza y'Uburundi, abo basirikare bapfiriye mu ntambara hagati y'Ubudagi n'Ububiligi, cane cane mu ndwano yabereye i Luvungi mu buseruko bwa Republika ya Demokarasi ya Congo.

Imva zigabuwe mu mirwi itatu nk'uko bisigurwa na Ndihokubwayo.

Uyu mwigisha avuga kandi ko izo mva zitarimwo gusa abasirikare b'Abadagi bapfiriye mu ntambara ya mbere y'isi yose. Ati: ''Muri zirya mva ziri mu Rugombo harimwo uruvangatirane. Umudagi wese yaba mu Burundi agapfa urwakarago bamujanye harya, umusirikare wese w'umudagi yapfiriye mu Burundi kuva 1905 kugeza mu 1918 ari harya.

"Eka n'abo basirikare b'Abanyafrika ahanini benshi bava muri Congo, Tanzania, Cameroun na Togo nabo nyene bahambwe harya, tutibagiye n'Abarundi babafashije mu kurwanya Ababirigi mu 1916".

Mu birori vyo kwibuka abo bantu vyabereye muri iryo tongo ry'abapfuye (akaburi) ku wa gatandatu, uwuserukira Ubudagi mu Burundi, Hubertus Klink, yavuze ko hibutswe abasirikare umunani b'Abadagi hamwe n'Abanyafrika 30 bapfiriye ku rugamba barwanira intwaro y'Ubudagi.

Abo bose bari mu ngabo z'Ubudagi zo muri Afrika y'Ubuseruko, zari zizwi nka Kaiserliche Schutztruppe für Deutsch-Ostafrika.

Ku bwa Hubertus Klink, guha icubahiro abo bahahambwe ni uburyo bwo gufasha abantu kumenya amateka.

"Nipfuza ko abantu bose bamenya kahise kugira dushobore kwubaka kazoza kacu n'ibihugu vyacu. Ivyo nabigize umwitwarariko wanje igihe nzoba nkiri hano mu Burundi."

Ubuserukizi bw'Ubudagi bwahora buja kwibuka abo basirikare ariko Hubertus Klink ubu yashatse ko uwo mugirwa umenyekana cane kurusha uko vyahora.

Ibirori vyo kwibuka vyabereye mu Rugombo vyari vyitabwe n'abaserukira ibihugu vyabo n'amashirahamwe mpuzamakungu, harimwo uwuserukira Ubumwe bwa Buraya mu Burundi, abaserukira Ubuholande na Tanzaniya, hamwe n'abasirikare bo muri Nigeria na Uganda bakorera mu Burundi.

Iryo tongo ryitwa Cimetière militaire allemand 1914-1918 riri hafi y'ibarabara rijana ku mipaka y'Uburundi, Congo n'Urwanda.

Nk'uko Ndihokubwayo abivuga, aho hantu hatowe kubera ko benshi mu bahahambwe baguye hafi y'aho.

"Kubona iryo tongo riri hafi y'umupaka wa Congo n'Uburundi ni uko benshi mu bahahambwe bapfiriye mu gitero c'Ababirigi cabereye i Luvungi mu 1916. Ntivyari vyoroshe ko bajanwa guhambwa kure cane y'aho baguye."

Imbere y'intambara ya mbere y'isi, Urwanda n'Uburundi vyari biri mu bukoroni bw'Ubudagi hamwe na Tanzania y'ubu mu cari kizwi nka Afrika y'Ubuseruko y'Abadagi (Afrique orientale allemande), mu gihe Congo yari icibare c'Umwami Leopod II w'Ababirigi.

Igihe iyo ntambara yaduka ku mugabane wa Buraya mu 1914, Ububirigi bwipfuza ko Congo itari kugira uruhara muri iyo ntambara.

Ariko ku wa 15 Myandagaro (8) 1914, ingabo z'Abadagi zaragavye ibitero ku birindiro vy'Ababirigi hafi y'ikiyaga Tanganyika, harimwo ahitwa Mokolobu, haca hakurikira n'ibindi bitero ahitwa i Lukuga.

Inyuma y'ivyo bitero, Ububirigi bwaciye bugomora ingabo zabwo za gikoloni, zari zizwi kw'izina rya Force Publique, kugira zirwanye Abadagi, ku bice vyose vyari bikoronijwe n'Ubudagi muri Afrika y'Ubuseruko.

Umwigisha Ndihokubwayo abandanya asigura ko Ababirigi batinjiye mu ntambara yo gufata Urwanda n'Uburundi kubera gusa ko bariko bararwanya Ubudagi. Hariho kandi inyungu za gisirikare, iza poritike, kwiyagurira akarere hamwe n'inyungu z'ubutunzi. Kimwe mu vyabatumye barwana kwari ugukingira Congo no kwitegurira kuronka ikibanza gikomeye mu biganiro vy'amahoro vyari gukurikira iyo ntambara.

Ingabo z'Ububirigi zafashe Urwanda muri Rusama (5) mu 1916, hanyuma zigarurira Uburundi muri Ruheshi (6) uwo mwaka nyene. Kuva ico gihe, ivyo bihugu bibiri vyaciye bitwarwa n'ubutegetsi bwa gisirikare bw'Ububirigi.

Hari amatariki atatu nyamukuru afasha gutahura uko ivyo vyagenze:

Ku bw'umwigisha Ndihokubwayo, ivyo rero bisigura ko Urwanda n'Uburundi bitahawe Ububirigi nk'ingabire y'ibihugu vyari vyatsinze intambara. Ahubwo vyavuye ku ngingo ya poritike mpuzamakungu yafashwe inyuma y'aho Ubudagi butsindiwe muri iyo ntambara.

The urn was placed in soil brought from different parts of Guatemala in a ceremony honouring the long-exiled poet, author and diplomat

The remains of writer and diplomat Miguel Ángel Asturias have been buried in his native Guatemala 52 years after he died in exile.

His ashes were brought to Guatemala from Paris, where he had lived before his death from cancer in the Spanish capital, Madrid, in 1974.

Asturias was awarded the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1967 for his vivid writings, which drew on the experiences of indigenous Guatemalans.

The urn containing his ashes was placed in soil gathered from different parts of Guatemala at a cultural centre named after him in Guatemala City.

His son, whose name is also Miguel Ángel Asturias, said at the ceremony on Sunday: "I can tell you, old man, that you are with us, you are in your homeland, you will sleep beneath your own skies."

Asturias, who was born in 1899, first moved to Paris in the 1920s to study ethnology.

Influenced by the surrealists, he wrote his first major work, Legends of Guatemala, a retelling of Maya origin legends and mythological tales, while in France.

Subsequent works, such as the 1946 novel The President and his Banana Trilogy, denounced the terrors of dictatorship in Latin America and the exploitation indigenous workers suffered on banana plantations.

Arguably his most famous novel was Men of Maize, published in 1949, which explores the struggles of indigenous communities as the world around them quickly changes and modernises.

Nobel Peace Prize laureate Rigoberta Menchú (centre) attended a ceremony to welcome the ashes of Asturias back to Guatemala alongside the writer's son (right)

Between 1944 and 1954, a period known as "Guatemala's 10 Years of Spring", he served in several diplomatic posts in Central and South America and continued writing.

But when the democratically elected Guatemalan President Jacobo Árbenz Guzmán was deposed in a CIA-backed coup in 1954, Asturias was stripped of his Guatemalan citizenship, his books were banned and he had to go into exile.

At Sunday's burial ceremony, Asturias's son said that the writer had "always wanted to be in Guatemala" but "political conditions did not allow him to".

The family only agreed to have the ashes moved from Père Lachaise cemetery in Paris to Guatemala after the current progressive president of Guatemala, Bernardo Arévalo, was elected in 2023.

Arévalo praised Asturias at the interment ceremony as "our voice in the world".

"He deserved to rest in the land he named and reinvented in his pages," said Arévalo, whose father Juan José appointed Asturias to the diplomatic service when the older Arévalo served as president during the 10 Year Spring.

In July Riad Bouchaker was found guilty of the eight charges he faced

A 52-year-old man has been sentenced to life in prison for the attempted murder of three children outside a primary school in Dublin's Parnell Square in November 2023.

Riad Bouchaker, of no fixed address, was also found guilty of assault causing serious harm to creche worker Leanne Flynn, and of assaulting two other children and a teenager.

On Monday, Judge Tony Hunt imposed the overall sentence of life imprisonment in Dublin's Central Criminal Court.

Rioting across many parts of Dublin following the attack led to the deployment of the most riot police in Irish history.

Bouchaker was originally from Algeria but had lived in Ireland for 25 years prior to the attack, and he had Irish citizenship.

He was assisted by an Arabic interpreter and a speech-and-language expert during the trial, who were present in court for the sentencing.

The attack took place outside a primary school on Parnell Square East

The attack took place outside Gaelscoil Choláiste Mhuire in Parnell Square, shortly after 13:40 local time on 23 November.

A group of 13 children, aged five and six, were lined up on Parnell Square waiting to go to their afterschool provision. Childcare worker Leanne Flynn was helping a little boy zip up his jacket when Bouchaker pulled his knife on the children.

A five-year-old girl was left with a lifelong brain injury after being stabbed in the heart.

Now eight, she is non-verbal and can only communicate by blinking, uses a wheelchair and has to be fed through a tube in her stomach as she cannot swallow safely by herself.

The judge said the child will never live independently and that her life, and the lives of her family, had been permanently altered.

He also noted that Flynn suffered life-threatening injuries, including a collapsed lung and the loss of a spleen, as well as profound psychological consequences and her services not being available to children.

The judge said she had acted fearlessly to protect the children and hoped she could return to work in the future, but said the possibility of such remains an unanswered question.

Judge Hunt said this was an unprecedented, highly unusual case involving a sudden, ferocious, sustained attack on young children and their childcare worker.

He said he had to mark the exceptional gravity of the offending against very young children and their carer, with a lethal weapon leading to consequences of the utmost gravity.

He said the circumstances were uniquely horrific and marked a profound assault on the most fundamental values protected by the criminal law.

The judge said the children happened to be selected because they were there and he was not yet sure what inference could be drawn from how Bouchaker found himself at their collection point.

At an earlier hearing, the court heard he received brain surgery in 2021 and a portion of his skull was removed, leaving a part of his brain vulnerable.

He suffered a head injury when members of the public intervened during the Parnell Square attack, after which he received hospital treatment for a month.

His defence team, which the judge ordered cannot be named due to safety concerns, said Bouchaker's cognitive function, memory, concentration, communication and decision-making were affected as a result of the impairment.

The most riot police in Irish state history were deployed to deal with the rioting following the attack

The attack was followed by riots across much of Dublin .

The most riot police in Irish state history were deployed to deal with the unrest.

Within hours of the attack, rioters destroyed 11 police vehicles, while 13 shops were badly damaged and more were looted during clashes with riot police.

Three buses and a tram were also destroyed and several police officers were injured during three hours of sustained violence.

Ireland's police chief at the time, Drew Harris blamed the rioting on a "lunatic, hooligan faction driven by a far-right ideology".

MN202611_1qdnyi5guyz.t:
A statue of William Shakespeare in his birthplace Stratford-upon-Avon

The director of the Shakespeare Institute has said he will resign if plans to move the centre from Stratford-upon-Avon to Birmingham go ahead.

Professor Michael Dobson said he was "very unhappy" with the University of Birmingham's decision to relocate the postgraduate research institute from its historic home at Mason Croft to the university's Edgbaston campus in September 2027.

"Stratford has been the place where people come to dream of Shakespeare since the 18th Century," he said.

The Shakespeare Institute announced on Facebook on Friday that it had been informed it would leave Stratford after more than 75 years. The future of Mason Croft, along with its historic garden and playing fields, has not yet been confirmed.

The University of Birmingham said the move was "an academic decision" rather than a cost-cutting measure and insisted Shakespeare studies remained a priority.

It added it would consult the Royal Shakespeare Company, the Shakespeare Birthplace Trust, local representatives and the wider community in the coming weeks.

However, Dobson rejected the university's characterisation of the decision.

"It affects academics, but it's not an academic decision in which anybody who works on Shakespeare at the University of Birmingham wishes to agree or go along with," he said.

"For 75 years Birmingham has been the only university in the world teaching and studying Shakespeare in Shakespeare's hometown," he said.

"That gives it enormous symbolic capital and has done wonders for the university's visibility and reputation in the humanities."

Dobson said Stratford was "the focus of the world's love of Shakespeare" and claimed the institute helped keep the town on the "intellectual and scholarly map" as well as its tourist and theatrical map.

The Shakespeare Institute was founded in 1951 at the Mason Croft building in Stratford-upon-Avon

He also questioned claims the move would help attract students.

"I think it will lose students," he said.

"Imagine you've moved your entire life to Stratford-upon-Avon to spend three years writing a thesis using our unique research library, and you're suddenly told the Institute is moving to rooms we haven't even seen in Birmingham.

"It takes a long time to box up, move and reorder 60,000 books."

The University of Birmingham said the move to relocate the centre was "an academic decision"

The Shakespeare Institute, which celebrated its 75th anniversary in July, has worked with academics, writers and performers for decades, including Dame Judi Dench.

Meanwhile, a petition calling on the university to reverse its plans has been signed by thousands of people. , external

The campaign urges the university to keep the Institute at Mason Croft, its Grade II listed home since 1951. It also calls for the publication of the rationale, financial figures and equality impact assessments behind the proposal.

Campaigners argue relocating the Institute would damage Stratford's cultural and academic standing and threaten postgraduate Shakespeare studies in a town closely linked to both William Shakespeare and the Royal Shakespeare Company.
